newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair to unveil welfare plans.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair to unveil welfare plans.

text.p: British opposition Labour leader Tony Blair will unveil plans to get single mothers off benefit in a key speech on his plans for welfare reform on Friday.
Blair will tell a conference in the Netherlands that his plans, which would encourage single mothers to get jobs or training and help them with childcare, will save money.
Determined to neutralise Conservative party charges that it is still a tax and spend party, Labour said this week it would be tough on spending and keep taxes down if it took power.
Polls tip Labour to win the election which is due by May 22 at the latest.
Convinced that Conservative attacks on its tax and spend policy lost it the last election in 1992, Blair is determined not to make any spending commitments before the election.

An aide said on Thursday he was determined to break through the right-left stalemate that dominates debate on welfare reform, with the right believing poverty is unavoidable and the left convinced the market cannot work.

Blair is expected to return to his favoured themes of rights and responsibilities, attacking the ruling Conservatives for dividing society into the haves and have-nots, but warning that people must be prepared to work if they want state help.

The speech is likely to be controversial. Right-wing Conservatives accuse single mothers of bringing their problems on themselves while left-wingers in the Labour party accuse the government of picking on defenceless women and children.

Britain has one million single mothers on income support, and far fewer single mothers working than in neighbouring states. Blair is expected to call for tax relief for employers taking on the long-term unemployed, including single mothers.
He is also expected to announce plans for after-school clubs for children, improved childcare and a relaxation of rules which mean single mothers lose welfare benefits if they study.
